blocks.title: This router cannot be managed yet
What to do
lines: Something the module cannot work without is missing or unreachable, so no live figures are collected. Module settings lists every readiness check, with what each missing piece costs.
The install form on that page only appears once this blocking problem is cleared, because none of the pieces that block a router this way can be installed from here.

blocks.title: Waiting for the router
lines: This page fills in as soon as the router answers. Connect to it as root over SSH from the machine list; nothing is collected until then.
Nothing is wrong yet - the readiness checks have simply not run.

blocks.title: Nothing has been read off this router yet
lines: The machine is connected and the readiness probe is running. Until it answers there is no sample to draw, so every tile on this page would be a zero the module invented rather than a figure the router gave it.
The probe repeats about every thirty seconds while this page is open. Check now asks immediately; if it never gets past this, Module settings names what the router is failing to answer.

blocks.title: Working, but not everything is available
lines: The figures below are real. Something optional is missing, so part of the automation is unavailable - Module settings names it and offers to install it where it can.

blocks.title: The numbers below are frozen
lines: The fast probe has stopped producing samples, so everything on this page is the last good reading rather than the router's current state.
Reason below is what the last attempt returned. Refresh now, in the Router section, retries immediately; if it keeps failing, check that the machine entry is still connected over SSH.

blocks.title: Compatibility mode: no Bored Manager agent on this router
lines: Everything on this page is real and everything below still works. The module is driving the router over SSH, the way it always has.

What is missing is the safety net. A change that takes the connection down cannot undo itself, because there is nobody left on this side to tell it to; DHCP leases are read on a timer rather than as they happen; and a large PPPoE pool is written one round trip at a time.
Module settings, under Router packages, installs it - from a file on this machine when the router has no internet of its own.

blocks.title: Everything else on this page is still live
lines: The rest of the fast probe is answering, but the interface dump came back unreadable and the module is keeping the last list it could parse. The interface table, the WAN up and WAN error tiles, and every WAN state the automation reads are that old list, not the router's current one.

The usual cause is a pool large enough that the dump no longer fits in one answer. Raising the fast interval, in Settings, General, Update intervals, or shrinking the managed pool is what clears it; the module retries on its own every few ticks, so a one-off hiccup fixes itself.
Reason below is what the last attempt produced. Refresh now, in the Router section, asks for the dump again straight away.

blocks.title: How live data is collected
lines: WAN-pool traffic is aggregated on the router; per-session counters are deliberately not transferred.
At large interface counts the full interface dump runs every second or third fast tick, so WAN state can lag by up to three update cycles.
All live figures come from one batched SSH probe per tick. Its speed is an app setting rather than a module one: Settings, General, Update intervals.
History is read back from disk, at whatever Chart sample interval is set under Module settings, Display & charts. The live tiles above the charts do not wait for it - they move on every fast tick.

What this needs
lines: The capacity report arrived with router packages 2.4.0. Everything else on this module keeps working without it, and Router limits under Module settings still reads and writes this router's conntrack and neighbour tables.
Nothing has been read yet. This tab asks the router once a minute while it is open.

blocks.title: This report has aged
lines: This report is more than five minutes old. The numbers below describe the router as it was; press Refresh before acting on them. A fix is refused against a report this old.

blocks.title: Reading this tab
lines: Every number here is an estimate worked out on the router itself, from what it has and what its configuration asks of it - not a measurement and not a promise. The ceiling is where it is expected to stop being stable, and the row beside it names what runs out first. The four tiers say how the requirements change as the router grows. A Fix button appears only where this module already has a way to write that change, and the row says exactly what it writes and who writes it.

rowActions.label: Fix
rowActions.confirm: Apply this fix on the router now? The row says exactly what is written and who writes it, and the report is asked again afterwards. A fix that reloads the firewall briefly interrupts new connections.

blocks.title: Reading these charts
lines: The right-hand edge is live - it comes from the same fast sweep as the tiles on the Overview tab. Everything behind it is read back from the metrics history on disk.

How coarse that history is, is a setting: Module settings, Display & charts, Chart sample interval. At its default of 60 seconds a one-hour chart holds about sixty archived points, which is why a short window can look like a staircase.
A range only reaches as far back as the app keeps history for. That cap is in the app's own Settings, under Data & storage.

blocks.title: Reassign and Unassign need an instance behind the device
lines: Both act through the WAN Binding instance that owns the device's LAN. Group by binding state, or read the Binding column: a row marked unmanaged has no instance behind it, and both buttons refuse it and say so.
To bring a LAN under management, create an instance for it on the Connection page, under WAN Binding.

rowActions.label: Reassign
rowActions.confirm: Give this device a different WAN on the next sweep? Its current session is dropped. A device marked unmanaged has no binding instance behind it and is refused.

rowActions.label: Unassign
rowActions.confirm: Take this device's WAN away and leave it waiting? It keeps local access but has no internet route. A device marked unmanaged has no binding instance behind it and is refused.

blocks.title: A waiting device has no internet route
lines: Reason says why each one is still waiting, across every binding instance on this router. Waiting for a free WAN clears itself when one comes back; unassigned by hand needs Reassign; preferences exhausted means the instance ran out of ip rule priorities and no WAN coming free will help - the room it has is the gap between Assignment rule priority base and Catch-all rule priority base, on Connection, WAN Binding, Daemon settings, and an instance already on the router keeps the numbers it was created with.

lines: Managed PPPoE sessions are never listed here - there can be thousands of them, and they are summarised by the WAN pool tiles above instead. The interfaces that are left are capped as well, because the whole payload has a per-tick size budget.
Not listed below counts both: every managed pool session, plus anything past that cap. When it is large, the router shell on Module settings is the way to read the full list.
